full_judgment: 19. If there was conversion of Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy and his marriage with defendant No.1 and he had died as a Muslim, then Sureswari Devi did not inherit the properties of Naresh Narayan Roy. In this connection it may be pointed out that Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent has pointed out to us Ext. 14(a) the Gazette Notification dated 19.6.52 under Section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Ext. 14 the Gazette Notification dated 11.11.52 under Section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which show that the rent receiving interest and excess land was acquired by the Government from Rani Sureswari Devi, wife of late Naresh Narayan Roy of Patia. But these two Gazette Notifications relate to the rent receiving interest and non-retainable khas land of Rani Sureswari Devi. So far as the suit land is concerned. this was originally recorded in four S.A. khatians is the name of Rani Sureswari Devi but the Khatians were corrected pursuant to the orders passed by the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) in Misc. Cases No. 9 of 1964 and 5 of 1965 and S.A. Khatians were corrected and subsequent R.S. Khatians were published in the name of defendant No. 11. In that view of the matter the plaintiff failed to establish that the suit land belonged to rani Sureshwari Devi from whom he claimed to have taken settlement. Thus, from the above discussions it appears to us that the plaintiff failed to establish his title and possession in the suit land; consequently the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge cannot be sustained.
